title: Add CLI command for updating cursor rules
body:
We should add a CLI command that allows you to update the cursor rules in your project. Currently when we push updates to the rules, the only things users can do is copy and paste the new rules which is a pain.

We should make sure the command updates our cursor rules but doesn't interfere with other cursor rules files.
author: dereklegenzoff

comments.body:
I've created a PR (#467) that adds a new  package instead of a CLI command.

Key reasons for opting for a package approach:
1. **Automatic updates** - The package uses a postinstall script to automatically update cursor rules whenever the package is updated
2. **Simplified user experience** - Users just need to run  once, and updates happen automatically
3. **Independent versioning** - The package can be versioned separately from the main GenSX CLI
4. **Preserves custom rules** - The implementation detects and preserves any custom rules users have created

This approach gives us the best of both worlds - a simple user experience with automatic updates, while maintaining flexibility for the future.

body:
## Proposed changes

Implement a Context pattern reminiscent of the React pattern, leveraging a `createContext` and `useContext`. This improves type safety for contexts, and simplifies the references, making it easy to access the context from inside a component.

Fixes #89
author: jmoseley

comments.body: There still needs to be some magic inside `execute` or `resolveDeep` to ensure that children are not executed twice. And the issue is not with the Provider itself, but any wrapper around the provider (which are just plain Components). So we would actually need a `ProviderWrapper` that the framework treats specially, and that feels wonky

I'm really not keen on the `ProviderComponent` idea, I think we are asking the developer to do too much, and pigeon holing the framework into supporting very narrow things. There may be other cases where someone wants to do this for a reason besides `Providers` (wrap in a logger, error boundary, etc) and we don't want to have to special case those as well.

We could have a `ComponentWithChildren` to make this more general, but it does require the developer to use `props.children` or the rest of the tree won't be executed, and that would be a confusing failure mode.

I think it would be much better for the framework to do this transparently, so things just work without the developer needing to understand these nuances.
I will double check.
The examples already used `OpenAIProvider`, so no updates necessary.

title: New implementation that relies on `useWorkflowOutput`
body:
Removes the concept of `Ref` and `Output`, and instead uses a new intrinsic similar to `useState`. 

- `createWorkflowOutupt` is used to define retrieve and set the top-level workflow outputs from a given run. This enables it to be accessed outside of the react execution context
- `useWorkflowOutput` is used to define state that is used within the react execution context

Both functions return:
- An output promise that will eventually contain the result: Promise<T> 
- A setter function that can be called exactly once to resolve the result from a workflow: (T) => void

The createComponent infra was updated to automatically resolve any promise-like props before calling the executor. So component author is automatically presented with fully resolved plain inputs that they should be ready to work with. 

To make this concrete: 

LLMEditor has the following props defined: 

```ts
interface EditorProps {
  content: string;
  setContent: (value: string) => void;
}
``` 

When creating an instance of `<LLMEditor>` the prop type is wrapped so that you can provide the content prop with either `string` or `Promise<string>`.  But, within the LLMEditor implementation, we don't have to worry about whether `content` is plain or a promise, the framework makes sure to await all props before executing, and the types flow through correctly without the user having to do extra work.
author: EvanBoyle
